prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” personal injury lawyer for every Chicago car-accident case — the right lawyer depends on factors like how serious your injuries are, whether liability is disputed, whether you’ll need litigation or a negotiated settlement, and your budget/comfort with the firm. That said, Chicago has many highly respected personal injury firms with strong experience handling car-accident claims.

Well-known Chicago personal injury firms you can consider (not an exhaustive or ranked list)
- Corboy & Demetrio
- Clifford Law Offices
- Levin & Perconti
- Power Rogers
- Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard
These firms have established personal injury practices and trial experience in serious car-accident cases.

How to pick the best attorney for your specific case
- Relevant experience: ask how many car-accident cases like yours they’ve handled and how many went to trial.
- Results: request examples of recent settlements or verdicts for similar injuries (they can’t guarantee results, but they can share representative outcomes).
- Who will handle the case: confirm whether the attorney you meet will do the work or whether it will be handed to a junior lawyer/paralegal.
- Communication: clarify response times and how you’ll receive updates.
- Fee structure: most PI lawyers work on contingency (typically ~33%–40% plus costs), and many offer free initial consultations.
- Trial readiness and reputation: look for a firm that will litigate if necessary — insurers often respond differently to lawyers who regularly try cases.
- Client reviews and disciplinary history: check Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers lists, Google/Yelp reviews, and the Illinois Attorney Registration & Disciplinary Commission.

Important practical items and timelines
- Illinois statute of limitations for most personal-injury claims is 2 years from the accident date (there are exceptions). Don’t delay contacting an attorney.
- Preserve evidence: photos, medical records, police report, witness contact info, vehicle damage.
- Seek medical care promptly and follow treatment — gaps can hurt your claim.
- Don’t post details about the crash or injuries on social media.

Questions to ask in a free consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? Results?
- Will you take my case on contingency? What percentage and who pays expenses?
- Who will handle the day-to-day work?
- What is your trial experience and how often do you go to trial?
- How long do cases like mine typically take?
- Can you provide references from past clients?

If you want, tell me:
- where in Chicago the crash happened,
- how badly you were injured,
- whether fault is disputed,
- and when the accident occurred —
and I can help narrow the list to firms that specialize in your type of case and suggest next steps for contacting them.
